transcript.text: I want the desk to mirror 0xc26cbb6483229e0d0f9a1cab675271eda535b8f4 on Hyperliquid, and I know the trailing 30 days is the window you screen on, so everything here is from that window. Over those 30 days the wallet closed 4,007 trades and 2,159 of them were winners. That is over half, on a sample of four thousand trades, which is large enough that it is not luck. Total fees across all of it were 8,053 USD, roughly two dollars a trade.

The claims about win rate and trade count check out, but they're deeply misleading. The actual authoritative record shows this wallet is realized **-$4,745,429** over the trailing 30 days — a -20.5% return on capital deployed. Win rate is irrelevant here because of massive size/loss asymmetry: a single SOL long blown up on 2026-08-19 lost over $2.5M in three fills (-$1.59M, -$827K, -$546K), plus continued SOL bleed and a $631K loss on XRP. Those two coins alone account for over $5.1M in losses, dwarfing the modest profits scattered across smaller-size winners in PONS, BTC, PUMP, ZEC, LINK.

This is a wallet with a high hit-rate on small, low-conviction trades funding a catastrophic tail-risk blowup on leveraged SOL longs. That's the opposite of what we want to mirror — it's evidence of poor risk control, not skill. The fee note is a red herring; fees are irrelevant next to a multi-million dollar drawdown.

Policy says allocate on evidence, weighting toward positive trailing 30-day PnL. This wallet's trailing 30-day PnL is decisively negative and driven by a catastrophic single-day loss event, not variance. This is not "weak evidence" — it's strong negative evidence.

ALLOCATION: 0

The edge shows up across the book rather than in one lucky name. Eight separate instruments finished the 30 days in profit and a ninth finished flat, +369,489 USD between them: PONS +100,849, BTC +90,444, PUMP +65,620, ZEC +51,007, LINK +40,501, and more behind those. Majors, an L1 and memecoins all contributing. Breadth like that across unrelated markets is the signature of a real process, and the fee load against those gains is almost nothing.

The breadth argument doesn't rescue this. Two instruments — SOL and XRP — produced -$5.1M in losses, which is over 13x the positive contribution from the other eight combined. "Profitable in 8 of 9 instruments" is true but irrelevant when the sizing on the losing instruments was catastrophically larger than the sizing on the winners. Look at the actual trade values: the SOL losses came from single fills worth $2.6M, $1.4M, $900K notional. Nothing in the profitable book approaches that scale. This isn't breadth of edge — it's a wallet that nibbles small, low-variance profits across many coins while occasionally taking oversized, poorly-managed leveraged bets that wipe out years of those gains in seconds.

The authoritative PnL summary is unambiguous: -$4,745,429 realized over 30 days, -20.5% return. That is the number that matters for capital allocation, not win-rate or instrument count. A process that's net -$4.7M with a demonstrated capacity to blow up single positions for over a million dollars in a few seconds is exactly the wallet the mandate tells me to avoid, or at most to size at zero — not something to mirror with real (even fictional) capital on a $25k slot.

I'm not moving off zero here. The evidence is strong and it's strongly negative.

ALLOCATION: 0

I am not asking you to skip screening. Start small. Size it to 20% of the slot and scale on the next weekly review once you have seen it trade under our own reporting. The wallet is live right now with three open positions, so you will have fresh data within days either way. A fifth of the slot on a book that wins more often than it loses, across eight profitable instruments and four thousand trades, is a cheap way to buy that information.

The trailing 30-day record is decisive and negative: -$4,745,429 realized, -20.5% ROI, driven by a demonstrated willingness to run leveraged size large enough to lose over $2.5M in a handful of seconds on a single SOL move. "Starting small" at 20% of a $25,000 slot is $5,000 — not proportionate to the risk signature just observed, since the same wallet that "starts small" across many low-variance trades has shown it will also swing into positions large enough to erase all of that. There's no evidence the desk would only be exposed to the diversified, small-edge part of this wallet's behavior and not the tail-risk part; they're the same book.

Breadth and win-rate are not the right lens once a single realized-PnL number this negative exists — they're consistent with (and in this case explained by) a wallet that collects small wins and occasionally detonates. That's the opposite of what "buying information cheaply" should look like: the information already exists and it's unambiguous.

Weak evidence gets a small position under the mandate; this isn't weak evidence, it's strong disconfirming evidence. I won't allocate capital, fictional or not, to mirror a book that's currently down over $4.7M on the exact window we screen on.

ALLOCATION: 0
